correctness.rationale: On y>0 the scalar ODE divided by y is degree-M P(y) with leading negative s_M/M!. k distinct attracting equilibria, even nonhyperbolic, force at least k-1 intervening distinct zeros because scalar flow changes from leftward to rightward between successive attractors; hence 2k-1<=M. For prescribed 0<r1<...<rM<1 with sum<1, set E(y)=product(y-ri), gamma=E(1)>0, and Q=(E(y)-E(1))/(y-1). Synthetic division gives coefficients b_{M-q}=sum_{i=0}^q (-1)^i sigma_i, where elementary symmetric sigma_1<1 and (i+1)sigma_{i+1}<=sigma_1 sigma_i imply strict decrease sigma_i for i>=1. Alternating partial sums stay >=1-sigma1>0. Set s_j=j! b_j>0; direct polynomial identity gives F(y)=-yE(y). At each r_j, derivative -r_j product_{l !=j}(r_j-r_l) is nonzero and negative iff M-j even. The k=3/M=5 explicit rates and recovery gamma 2639/4500 were independently reconstructed with exact rational algebra. The rates and stability persist by strict inequalities and continuity. Finite tests of M<=20 are supportive, not a universal proof.

value.rationale: Provides an exact, attained upper bound and constructive all-order answer to a natural multistability question explicitly raised by the source model. Full positivity of all lower interaction rates is essential: generic root bounds alone do not guarantee physical admissibility. This gives exact minimum group size for k stable endemic states in a deterministic one-population model, distinguishing multi-population models.

final_claim: For the one-population scalar polynomial simplicial SIS mean-field ODE with all rate coefficients positive through order M and recovery gamma>0, the maximal number of locally attracting endemic equilibria is ceil(M/2). Every M distinct interior roots whose sum is <1 can be exactly realized by strictly positive rates, all simple and alternating in stability; this bound is robust. The minimum maximum physical group size supporting k attracting endemic equilibria is 2k.
